item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate B follows the frozen contract’s intended composition: build the multipart payload with the established helper, then pass it through the unchanged Add method. Candidate A has stronger retry-body assertions, but changes Add’s behavior and bypasses it from Upload.","reasons":["B preserves FilesService.Add unchanged, while A eagerly buffers every Add body, changing streaming, memory, timing, and reader-error semantics contrary to the requirement to preserve Add behavior.","B routes Upload directly through s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), exactly preserving centralized option handling, request construction, decoding, and errors.","B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with the required field name and filename and performs pre-request filename/content validation.","A introduces a private add path and has Upload call it directly, duplicating the Add routing boundary the contract explicitly requires Upload to reuse."],"risks_a":["The new io.ReadAll in Add can impose substantial memory use on arbitrary caller-built multipart bodies and changes when source-reader failures occur.","Upload precomputes filesOptions and bypasses Add, creating two entry paths whose validation and behavior can drift.","Although A’s retry test verifies multipart content on both attempts, that test coverage does not justify the contract violations in production code."],"risks_b":["The retry test does not inspect the multipart body on either attempt, so it does not directly prove that streamed content is replayed intact.","The retry test omits RetryAllMethods: true, making it less faithful to the reported POST-retry configuration.","Visible tests do not cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader errors, despite the contract requesting those cases."]}
